name: Constanța
title: Constanța Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement and Hull Gauging
description: Ship thickness measurement in Constanța and Midia: hull structure gauging for bulk carriers and tankers, ESP renewal survey support and pre-docking UTM.
h1: Ship Thickness Measurement in Constanța and the Romanian Black Sea Ports
intro: Constanța is the largest port on the Black Sea and the sea gate for Danube river traffic, so a superintendent with a ship there may be looking after anything from a grain-laden bulk carrier to a river-sea coaster or a tanker at Midia. A team travels from India to Constanța for dock stays at Constanța Shipyard, berth calls and anchorage waits, and the gauging is planned against the ship's survey or vetting requirement.

highlights.p: Constanța Shipyard builds and repairs ships inside the port. Gauging during a dock stay there reaches bottom shell, bilge and side plating, and the steel list can be settled from measured figures early in the stay rather than from estimates.

The Danube–Black Sea Canal enters the port at Agigea, bringing river-sea ships and barge convoys alongside ocean bulk carriers. River-sea hulls are built to lighter scantlings, so wastage uses up their margin sooner, and gauging shows how much remains.

North of Constanța at Năvodari, Midia port serves the Petromidia refinery. Tankers calling there can be gauged on deck, in the ballast tanks and along the deck lines around cargo work, as preparation for vetting or a CAP survey.

port.h: Constanța: the Black Sea's largest port and its traffic
p: Constanța's port stretches along the coast from the older northern basins near the city centre to the newer southern area at Agigea, where the Danube–Black Sea Canal reaches the sea. That geography explains the traffic. Ocean-going bulk carriers bring in ores and coal and load grain; container ships use the terminals in the south of the port; tankers and chemical carriers work the liquid-bulk berths; and river-sea ships and Danube barge convoys move cargo between the sea and an inland waterway that runs deep into central Europe. Romanian grain exports, and since 2022 Ukrainian grain routed through Romania, have kept the grain terminals under steady pressure.

Waiting time is the gauging opportunity. In the grain season, bulk carriers can spend days at the anchorage off Constanța waiting for a loading slot, and ships bringing cargo for transhipment to barges may wait for river capacity. Those idle periods suit ballast tank, hatch cover and deck gauging by launch, and once a ship has discharged, its empty holds can be gauged before it loads again. Ships that need repair have Constanța Shipyard within the port, so a survey item found on arrival can turn into a planned dock stay without the ship leaving the area.

Inspection demand at Constanța reflects that mix. Older bulk carriers in Black Sea and Mediterranean trades come up for their third and fourth renewal surveys, when the gauging of transverse bulkheads, hold frames and the hopper and topside tank structure becomes extensive. Tankers at Midia and in the port face vetting and CAP expectations from charterers. River-sea ships need gauging that respects their thinner plating and smaller margins. Offshore gas development in the Romanian sector of the Black Sea is also bringing offshore support and construction vessels into the port, each with its own hull, tank and piping inspection needs between campaigns.

facilities.h: Where gauging happens in Constanța and along the Romanian coast
p: Constanța Shipyard, inside the port, is the main place for in-dock gauging on the Romanian coast. A docking there gives access to bottom shell, bilge plating and sea chests, and the staging the yard rigs for hold and tank repairs gives reach to upper frames and deckheads that are otherwise hard to measure. The most useful gauging is done early in the docking, so that the yard, the owner and the class surveyor work from one set of figures when they agree what is cropped and renewed on the steel list.

Most other work is afloat. The terminals across the port offer alongside access for bulk carriers, tankers and container ships between cargo operations, with gate passes arranged through the agent, while the outer anchorage holds ships waiting for berths. Midia, a short distance north, adds refinery tanker berths, and Mangalia, to the south, is a further port on the same coast. River-sea ships calling at Constanța can be gauged alongside at whichever berth they work, with the measurement grid adjusted to their lighter scantlings and to the class notation they trade under.
list: Constanța Shipyard — shipbuilding and repair yard within the port; a docking here opens up bottom, bilge and sea chest areas for a full renewal-survey gauging programme.
Constanța South and Agigea — container terminals and the Danube–Black Sea Canal entrance; deck and tank gauging on container ships and river-sea traffic alongside.
Bulk berths across the port — grain, ore, coal and general cargo; the turnaround between cargoes leaves holds open for frame, hopper and tank-top readings.
Midia port, Năvodari — refinery tanker berths serving Petromidia; deck, ballast tank and deck-pipeline gauging during cargo operations, under terminal rules.
Constanța anchorage — ships queuing for grain and other berths; boarding by launch for ballast tank, hatch cover and deck measurements.

context.h: Romanian port state control, EU rules and Black Sea conditions
p: Romania carries out port state control through the Romanian Naval Authority and, as an EU member, takes part in the Paris MoU as well as the Black Sea MoU. Ship age and type feed into the risk profile that sets how often a ship is inspected, so an ageing bulk carrier or tanker calling regularly at Constanța should expect expanded inspections. For ESP ships, preparation means more than the hull itself: the survey report file, the latest thickness measurement reports and the condition evaluation report must be on board and current, because an inspector who finds them missing or out of date has a reason to look harder at the structure.

Romanian waters of the Black Sea carry no ECA designation, but EU rules take over alongside: a 0.10% sulphur ceiling for ships at berth unless an abatement method is used, the EU ETS on voyages to and from Constanța since 2024, and FuelEU Maritime from 2025. Romania's full accession to Schengen in January 2025 means a team travelling from India needs a Schengen visa. Since 2022, drifting mines have been reported in the western Black Sea, and Romania, Bulgaria and Turkey set up a joint mine-countermeasures group in 2024. Routing and war-risk cover follow the owner's and underwriters' advice, and in-port gauging is scheduled within that guidance.

jobs.p: Work in Constanța comes from three directions: ocean bulk carriers in the grain and ore trades, tankers at Midia and at the port's liquid-bulk berths, and the river-sea fleet using the canal. The scenarios below show how a gauging attendance fits each of them, from a full renewal-survey programme in dock to a short, targeted measurement during a cargo call.
list: Fourth renewal survey preparation on a supramax at Constanța Shipyard: transverse bulkheads, hold frames, hopper and topside tanks gauged before cropping, so the steel list and dock time are fixed early.
Tanker gauging at Midia during discharge for an ageing product tanker, measuring the deck plate, ballast tank structure and deck pipelines ahead of a CAP survey requested by a charterer.
River-sea ship thickness gauging alongside at Constanța for an owner deciding whether to renew steel or sell, with bottom and side plating read from inside the double bottom and holds.
Empty-hold gauging of a panamax bulk carrier between ore discharge and grain loading, re-measuring the areas of substantial corrosion recorded at its last survey.
Gauging for a prospective buyer of a general cargo ship lying at the anchorage, covering deck, hatch covers and accessible tanks so the purchase decision rests on measured figures.

logistics: International connections run through Bucharest Henri Coandă Airport, with road or rail transfer to the coast, and Mihail Kogălniceanu Airport near Constanța has a smaller schedule of flights. The shipyard and the port terminals are ISPS-controlled, so the ship's agent applies for access permits covering each technician and the gauges, using passport details sent ahead, and books launches for anchorage boardings. Because Romania is in the Schengen area, the India-based team needs Schengen visas; we start the application once the docking or ETA window is firm and keep the owner informed of the visa timeline.

faqs.q: Do you cover ship inspection in Romania outside Constanța?
faqs.a: Yes. The same mobilisation can take in Midia and Mangalia on the Romanian coast and continue south to Varna and Burgas in Bulgaria, all within the Schengen area. For river-sea ships, attendance further up the Danube can be planned case by case, depending on where the ship lies and what access the berth allows.

faqs.q: Can holds be gauged on a bulk carrier waiting at the Constanța anchorage?
faqs.a: Only if they are empty. A ship waiting to load grain is the ideal case: the holds are clean and dry, and frames, hopper plating and bulkheads can be measured before the first cargo goes in. A laden ship waiting to discharge offers ballast tanks, the deck and the hatch covers instead, with hold work left until after discharge.

faqs.q: How is thickness measurement in Romania different on a river-sea ship?
faqs.a: The principle is the same, but the margins are smaller. River-sea ships are built to lighter scantlings, so the same loss of plate represents a larger share of the allowable margin, and the measurement grid needs care around localised wastage. We set the gauging points against the class requirements for the ship's notation and survey, not against ocean-going norms.

faqs.q: Is hull gauging in Constanța affected by the Black Sea security situation?
faqs.a: Work alongside and at anchor is planned within the owner's security guidance. The situation since 2022 has mainly affected routing, war-risk cover and transit planning rather than gauging in port. The team reaches Constanța by air, through Bucharest or the local airport, and we confirm arrangements with the ship's agent before travel.
